title: Orbit and Terminal
premise: Noor Thackeray has spent eleven years alone tending the Svalbard seed vault and its mysterious beacon, a signal she inherited from a predecessor who vanished. When the ship Meridian returns from a forty-year deep-space voyage with its crew biologically younger than when they left, Noor discovers her beacon was the thing that called them home—and that Earth's two surviving orbital factions each claim the right to decide which cryo-pods wake first. As the fleet's fragile truce collapses around her, Noor learns the beacon's true purpose: it was built to choose, using genetic archives only she can access. In the end, Noor refuses to choose either faction alone, broadcasting the vault's full archive to both sides and forcing humanity to wake everyone together or lose the seeds—and each other—forever.
about_author: Rosalind Quintana is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing agricultural seed collections across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes near-future science fiction about the people history forgets to mention.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Cold Seeds
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet her solitary routine in the Arctic vault: checking germination rates, logging the beacon's nightly pulse, talking to jars of wheat like old friends. A routine diagnostic reveals the beacon has been transmitting an encrypted handshake for months—something is answering. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The ship Meridian breaches atmosphere unannounced, landing on the ice plain below the vault. Its crew steps out impossibly young—faces Noor recognizes from pre-departure records as forty years older. Their captain, Ilsa Reyes, claims the beacon summoned them home early. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Inside Meridian, we learn the truth: the crew entered cryosleep for a generation-long survey and woke decades too soon, their cells reversed by an anomaly they can't explain—anomaly readings that match the beacon's frequency exactly. Ilsa hides this from her crew. Emotional beat: guilt and protective secrecy.

chapters.title: Two Flags Over the Ice
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Word of Meridian's return reaches the orbital factions—the Concord and the Verity Compact—who dispatch rival delegations to the vault, each claiming custody of the returned crew and the beacon. The fleet truce, already fraying, gives them ninety days to resolve succession of the cryo-archive. Emotional beat: Noor's home becoming contested ground.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Digging into the vault's founding records with Noor, Ilsa discovers the beacon was commissioned by the same consortium that built the cryo-fleet—a selection protocol designed to rank human genomes for priority waking. Noor realizes her whole custodianship was a lie of omission. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Both factions issue ultimatums: hand over the selection archive or be declared hostile. Sabotage strikes Meridian's reactor; a Concord envoy is found frozen outside the perimeter. Noor and Ilsa, increasingly allied, have weeks—not months. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a vise.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor decrypts the full archive and finds the impossible: the ranking list includes her own name at the top, placed there by her vanished predecessor—her predecessor was her mother, and the beacon chose her long ago. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade; belonging revealed as design.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Small Country
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa is ordered by her own faction to seize the archive by force, and must choose between the crew who trust her and the truth about the anomaly—that the beacon didn't just call them home, it may have caused their reversal deliberately, as a test. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Noor's POV (climax). With the truce hours from expiry and armed shuttles descending, Noor transmits the entire genome archive openly to both fleets, erasing any faction's monopoly on choice. Ilsa refuses the seizure order publicly, turning her crew's guns aside. The factions must now negotiate over shared data or destroy the vault and everything in it. Emotional beat: terrifying, liberating refusal.

chapters.title: Germination
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue-like. Months later, under a brokered accord, the first joint waking begins—pods opening in pairs, one from each faction's lists, Noor's own name struck from the record by her own hand. Spring comes late to the ice; the first test crop goes into thawed ground. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; belonging chosen rather than assigned.
